rulebook.statement: The record performance must be measured by automatic officiating equipment. Semi-automatic equipment is acceptable only when the automatic system malfunctions.
rulebook.plain: A watch-only time is not enough for these world-record provisions; the stated electronic backup exception requires an automatic-system failure.

rulebook.title: Salt content and no sea-water records
rulebook.statement: The water must contain less than 3 grams of salt per litre. A performance in sea or ocean water cannot qualify.
rulebook.plain: The threshold is strictly below 3 g/L, and the rule separately excludes all sea or ocean water.

rulebook.title: Competition swim or publicly announced time trial
rulebook.statement: The performance must occur in ordinary competition or in a publicly held individual race against the clock advertised at least three days beforehand. The advance-advertising condition does not apply to a time trial sanctioned by a member federation during a competition.
rulebook.plain: A separate record attempt normally needs public access and three days’ public notice; the named federation-sanctioned competition time-trial exception removes the advertising requirement.

rulebook.title: Certify the actual record lane length
rulebook.statement: The length of the particular lane used for the performance must be certified by a surveyor or another qualified official appointed or approved by the member federation of the country where the pool is located.
rulebook.plain: Certification must cover the lane in which the record was swum, not merely an assumed pool length.

rulebook.title: Recheck a movable-bulkhead course after the session
rulebook.statement: If the course uses a movable bulkhead, the record lane’s length must be confirmed at the end of the session in which the swim took place by a surveyor or other qualified official appointed or approved by the host-country member federation.
rulebook.plain: A movable wall requires the specified end-of-session length confirmation.
rulebook.issue: The source sentence repeats its final confirmation phrase. Its requirement is restated once here without adding a different measurement deadline.

rulebook.title: Anti-doping sample deadline for record recognition
rulebook.statement: For an individual record, a sample must be collected from the swimmer immediately after the performance or, at the latest, within 24 hours after the race ends, and the analysis must be negative. For a relay record, samples must be collected from all four swimmers in the finals relay team within the same immediate-to-24-hour window, and every analysis must be negative.
rulebook.plain: The record requirement includes timely sample collection and negative findings. The relay wording specifies all four members of the finals team; no further anti-doping procedures are invented here.

rulebook.title: Automatic approval at named WA events
rulebook.statement: Qualifying records achieved at the Olympic Games, World Aquatics Championships, World Aquatics Swimming Championships (25m), World Aquatics Junior Swimming Championships or World Aquatics Swimming World Cups are approved automatically only when all record conditions have been met.
rulebook.plain: The named events have automatic approval, but the performance still has to meet every applicable record condition.

rulebook.title: Application route for records at other competitions
rulebook.statement: Records achieved outside the Olympic Games, World Aquatics Championships, World Aquatics Swimming Championships (25m), World Aquatics Junior Swimming Championships and Swimming World Cup must follow the application procedure in 12.5.1–12.5.4.
rulebook.plain: A record at another meet needs the formal reporting and application route.

rulebook.title: Provisional record notice within seven days
rulebook.statement: An authorised representative of the meet’s management committee must send the Executive Director a written provisional record notification within seven days after the performance.
rulebook.plain: The first written notification has a seven-day deadline.

rulebook.title: Referee’s record application within fourteen days
rulebook.statement: Within fourteen days after the performance, the Referee must file the record application with the Executive Director using the official World Aquatics form and certify compliance with 12.3.
rulebook.plain: The formal application is the Referee’s responsibility and has a fourteen-day deadline.

rulebook.title: Review, declaration and publication of a record
rulebook.statement: On receiving the application, the Executive Director must assess compliance with 12.3. If the requirements are met, the record must be declared and published, and the relevant swimmers must receive diplomas.
rulebook.plain: Recognition follows the required review; the declaration and certificates follow a compliant application.

rulebook.title: Federation application when the meet procedure failed
rulebook.statement: If the management committee failed to follow all or part of the filing procedure, the swimmer’s member federation may submit an application on the official form. The Executive Director must assess compliance with 12.3 and, if satisfied, declare and publish the record and provide the relevant diplomas.
rulebook.plain: The federation has an alternative filing route when the meet’s process was not completed. This clause does not state an extra deadline or waive the record conditions.

rulebook.title: Diploma for an individual record
rulebook.statement: After approving an individual record, the Executive Director must send the swimmer’s member federation a diploma signed by the World Aquatics President for presentation to the swimmer.
rulebook.plain: The individual record certificate reaches the swimmer through their federation.

rulebook.title: Five diplomas for a relay record
rulebook.statement: After approving a relay record, the Executive Director must send the team’s member federation five diplomas signed by the World Aquatics President: one for the federation to keep and one for each of the four swimmers.
rulebook.plain: A recognised relay record receives a federation certificate plus four swimmer certificates.

rulebook.title: Additional record categories and target times
rulebook.statement: World Aquatics may create further World Record or World Junior Record categories with different strokes, distances or other variables. It must set a target time for a new category. A swim faster than that target may qualify, provided 12.3 is also met.
rulebook.plain: World Aquatics can introduce a new record category. Its initial target must be beaten, rather than merely equalled.

rulebook.title: Age range for the World Junior Championships
rulebook.statement: Eligibility for the World Aquatics Junior Swimming Championships requires an age of 14, 15, 16, 17 or 18 on 31 December of the year in which the competition starts.
rulebook.plain: For this championship, calculate age at the end of the competition’s starting year; race-day age is not the test.

rulebook.title: Age eligibility at the named senior championships
rulebook.statement: For the Olympic Games, World Aquatics Championships and World Aquatics Swimming Championships (25m), a swimmer must qualify through either the age route in 13.2.1 or the younger-swimmer standard in 13.2.2.
rulebook.plain: There are two alternative routes for these named events; meeting both is not required.

rulebook.title: Standard age route for named senior events
rulebook.statement: For the events covered by 13.2, a swimmer qualifies through this age route if they will be at least 14 on 31 December of the year in which the competition starts.
rulebook.plain: Turning 14 at any point in that calendar year meets this age condition; other event entry requirements still apply.

rulebook.title: Under-14 route using the B entry standard
rulebook.statement: A swimmer who will still be under 14 on 31 December of the competition’s starting year may qualify for an event under 13.2 if they have achieved at least that event’s B entry-time standard.
rulebook.plain: A younger swimmer needs the relevant event’s B standard for this exception. It is not an unrestricted age exemption.

rulebook.title: Domestic and other organisers may set age rules
rulebook.statement: Member federations and meet organisers may use these age rules, alternative rules, or a combination for competitions within their authority.
rulebook.plain: Do not assume that a local meet uses the World Championship age limits; its own applicable conditions must be checked.

rulebook.title: Permitted competition swimwear
rulebook.statement: A competitor must wear a swimsuit. Goggles and a cap are optional. Each item must meet the swimwear provisions in Part One, Article 6.
rulebook.plain: Wear an approved racing suit; goggles and a cap are allowed when they meet the governing swimwear requirements.

rulebook.title: No unauthorised performance aids
rulebook.statement: During competition, athletes must not use devices or swimwear that could assist speed, buoyancy or endurance, apart from swimwear permitted by the regulations. Examples include webbed gloves, fins and flippers. The August World Aquatics commentary identifies the adhesive-substance example as glue and expressly permits tape and nasal strips under this clause. Injury-taping provisions are addressed separately in 14.4.
rulebook.plain: Under the latest World Aquatics clarification, tape and nasal strips are permitted under this clause. This does not remove the ban on other unauthorised performance aids; injury taping is addressed in 14.4.
rulebook.issue: World Aquatics commentary dated 6 August 2026, p. 2, clarifies that the adhesive-substance wording refers to glue and permits tape and nasal strips under this clause. Specific English application of that August clarification has not been independently confirmed. The latest World Aquatics guidance is shown; this is not an unqualified English disqualification conclusion.

rulebook.title: Data collection without feedback
rulebook.statement: An automated device may be used solely to collect data. It must neither be able to send, nor be used to send, information, sound or signals to the competitor. It must also neither be able to assist, nor be used to assist, speed, flotation or endurance.
rulebook.plain: A recorder may collect information, but it cannot coach or signal to you during the race or provide a performance advantage.

rulebook.title: Injury tape: fingers, toes and other body parts
rulebook.statement: The February text permits injury-treatment or protection tape on one or two fingers or toes, including binding two together. The August World Aquatics commentary extends the stated permission to tape used to treat or protect injuries on other parts of the body. It does not create a general permission to use any tape for performance assistance.
rulebook.plain: The latest World Aquatics guidance allows injury-protection tape beyond fingers and toes. The local application of that August clarification still needs checking for England.
rulebook.issue: World Aquatics commentary dated 6 August 2026, p. 2, explicitly extends injury-treatment/protection taping to other body parts. English application of that August clarification has not been independently confirmed. The narrow February wording and later guidance are both shown.

rulebook.title: 50 m racing distance with touch panels
rulebook.statement: Where automatic timing touch panels are fitted at either or both ends of a 50 m pool, the pool construction must preserve the required 50.000 m racing distance between the effective end surfaces.
rulebook.plain: Measure the course with the touch panels in their racing positions, rather than assuming the bare pool length is the racing length.

rulebook.title: 25 m racing distance with touch panels
rulebook.statement: Where automatic timing touch panels are fitted at either or both ends of a 25 m pool, the pool construction must preserve the required 25.000 m racing distance between the effective end surfaces.
rulebook.plain: Touch panels take up space. The short-course racing distance must still be 25 m after they are installed.

rulebook.title: 50 m length tolerance
rulebook.statement: With touch panels fitted, the permitted 50.000 m course tolerance is zero shortfall and an excess no greater than 0.010 m.
rulebook.plain: A measured long course may be up to 1 cm longer than 50 m, but cannot be shorter.

rulebook.title: 50 m wall spacing for panels at both ends
rulebook.statement: For a 50 m pool using automatic touch panels at both ends, the structural walls must be separated by 50.020–50.030 m.
rulebook.plain: Allow for a panel at each end when setting the wall-to-wall pool length.

rulebook.title: 50 m length throughout the measurement zone
rulebook.statement: The permitted course length must be maintained across the vertical zone from 0.300 m above the water to 0.800 m below it.
rulebook.plain: Checking only the waterline is insufficient; the required length applies above and below it.

rulebook.title: Certification of 50 m dimensions
rulebook.statement: The measurements must be certified by a surveyor or another qualified official appointed or accepted by the national member federation responsible for the pool location.
rulebook.plain: The long-course dimensions require qualified, federation-approved certification.

rulebook.title: 25 m length tolerance
rulebook.statement: With touch panels fitted, the permitted 25.000 m course tolerance is zero shortfall and an excess no greater than 0.010 m.
rulebook.plain: The measured short course may be up to 1 cm longer than 25 m, but cannot be shorter.

rulebook.title: 25 m wall spacing for two panels
rulebook.statement: For a 25 m pool with automatic touch panels at both ends, the structural walls must be 25.020–25.030 m apart.
rulebook.plain: The pool shell needs space for both panels while preserving the 25 m racing distance.

rulebook.title: 25 m wall spacing for one panel
rulebook.statement: For a 25 m pool with an automatic touch panel at only one end, the structural walls must be 25.010–25.020 m apart.
rulebook.plain: A one-panel setup has a different permitted wall-to-wall length from a two-panel setup.

rulebook.title: 25 m length throughout the measurement zone
rulebook.statement: The permitted course length must hold from 0.300 m above the water surface down to 0.800 m below it.
rulebook.plain: The short-course length must be correct through the whole specified vertical band.

rulebook.title: Recommended certification of 25 m dimensions
rulebook.statement: The measurements should be certified by a surveyor or another qualified official appointed or accepted by the national member federation responsible for the pool location.
rulebook.plain: This clause recommends qualified, federation-approved certification; its wording is “should”, rather than a mandatory instruction.

rulebook.title: Pool width at the Olympics and World Championships
rulebook.statement: At the Olympic Games and World Aquatics Championships, a permanent pool must be at least 25.000 m wide and a temporary pool at least 26.000 m wide.
rulebook.plain: These minimum widths apply to the named elite events, not automatically to every club meet.

rulebook.title: Pool width at other competitions
rulebook.statement: This provision sets no minimum overall pool width for competitions other than the Olympic Games and World Aquatics Championships.
rulebook.plain: No general minimum total width is specified here; separate lane-width requirements still exist.

rulebook.title: Depth at the Olympics and World Championships
rulebook.statement: The minimum depth at the Olympic Games and World Aquatics Championships is 2.5 m.
rulebook.plain: The named long-course elite events need a pool at least 2.5 m deep.

rulebook.title: Depth at the 25 m World Championships
rulebook.statement: For the World Aquatics Swimming Championships (25m), the pool must be at least 2.0 m deep; a depth of 2.5 m is recommended.
rulebook.plain: For this event, 2.0 m is mandatory and 2.5 m is the recommendation.

rulebook.title: Depth at other World Aquatics events
rulebook.statement: At other World Aquatics Events the minimum pool depth is 1.0 m. When starting blocks are used, a depth of at least 1.35 m is required through the zone from 1.0 m to at least 6.0 m from the end wall.
rulebook.plain: The block-start depth zone has a stricter minimum than the remaining pool. This clause expressly concerns World Aquatics Events.

rulebook.title: End-wall geometry and grip
rulebook.statement: End walls must be solid, upright, parallel, and perpendicular to both the course and water surface. The non-slip finish must reach at least 0.8 m below the water so turns are safe. A deviation of up to 0.3 degrees from vertical is allowed in either direction.
rulebook.plain: Swimmers need a stable, safe wall to touch and push against, with the specified alignment and underwater grip surface.

rulebook.title: Optional resting ledges
rulebook.statement: Resting ledges may be installed on pool walls at a depth of at least 1.2 m below the surface. They may be 0.10–0.15 m wide. Internal or external designs are allowed, with internal ledges preferred.
rulebook.plain: A submerged resting shelf is optional and must sit well below the racing surface; it is different from a backstroke starting ledge.

rulebook.title: Gutters and touch-panel clearance
rulebook.statement: Gutters are permitted on any pool wall and must have suitable protective covers. An end-wall gutter must allow touch panels to extend to the required height of 0.3 m above the water.
rulebook.plain: Drainage gutters must be safely covered and must not prevent the correct touch-panel installation.

rulebook.title: Olympic lane layout
rulebook.statement: The Olympic pool must provide eight 2.5 m lanes plus a 2.5 m rope-separated space outside each outer lane. A ninth and tenth lane may be used exceptionally with approval from the Technical Swimming Committee chair.
rulebook.plain: The standard Olympic racing layout uses eight lanes and outer buffer spaces; using extra lanes needs the specified approval.

rulebook.title: Ten lanes at World Championships
rulebook.statement: The World Aquatics Championships and the World Aquatics Swimming Championships (25m) require ten lanes.
rulebook.plain: The named World Championships use a ten-lane pool; the following clauses distinguish permanent and temporary pools.

rulebook.title: Permanent World Championship pool lanes
rulebook.statement: At the named World Championships, a permanent pool must have eight middle lanes 2.5 m wide and two outer lanes 2.4 m wide. A rope-separated gap of at least 0.1 m is required beyond each outer lane.
rulebook.plain: Permanent championship pools use slightly narrower outer lanes with an additional gap at each pool side.

rulebook.title: Temporary World Championship pool lanes
rulebook.statement: At the named World Championships, a temporary pool must provide ten lanes each 2.5 m wide, with a rope-separated gap of at least 0.5 m beyond each outer lane.
rulebook.plain: Temporary championship pools require ten full-width lanes and larger outside gaps.

rulebook.title: Lane layout at other competitions
rulebook.statement: Other competitions have no minimum lane count under this clause. Interior lanes must be at least 2.5 m wide; the first and last lanes must be at least 2.4 m wide, with an outside gap of at least 0.1 m on each side.
rulebook.plain: There is no universal lane count here, but the specified lane widths and outside spaces still apply within this WA facility standard.

rulebook.title: Lane-rope purpose
rulebook.statement: Lane ropes separate the lanes and reduce waves. Their design should lessen both wave transmission across the rope and reflection back towards its origin.
rulebook.plain: Ropes should absorb wave energy rather than simply marking the lane boundaries.

rulebook.title: Full-length lane ropes
rulebook.statement: A lane rope must cover the full racing course. At each end, parts that do not help suppress waves, including reels and springs, must occupy less than 200 mm.
rulebook.plain: Wave-reducing rope should run almost to the wall; inactive fittings have a strict length limit.

rulebook.title: Lane-rope anchoring
rulebook.statement: End-wall anchors should be recessed, and the installed rope should stay in the water. A deck-mounted anchor requires a rigid, non-stretch extension. The anchor and extension must project no more than 10 mm into the pool, and the permitted anchor-related change to rope length is at most 10 mm in either direction at each end.
rulebook.plain: Use stable fittings that keep the rope properly positioned. Recessed wall anchors are recommended; the projection and extension limits are mandatory.

rulebook.title: Wave elements, buoyancy and disputed diameter
rulebook.statement: The end anchors must hold the wave-reducing elements halfway below the water and withstand 20 kN tension. Along the course, between half and two-thirds of each element’s height must be submerged, with the rope specified as negatively buoyant. Float design should avoid changing rope length and should integrate a float between two discs. The printed diameter limits contradict one another, so no valid diameter range is asserted here.
rulebook.plain: The submersion, loading and design provisions can be read, but the diameter needs an official correction before a usable limit can be stated.
rulebook.issue: The February text describes 0.10 m as a maximum and 0.15 m as a minimum for the same diameter. Those limits cannot both be met. Do not silently reverse them or treat a guessed range as verified.

rulebook.title: Rope tensioning, spring and wire
rulebook.statement: The tensioning reel should require a tool to lock it and prevent unauthorised adjustment. A shock-absorbing tension spring is compulsory, and the wire must withstand 12 kN tensile loading.
rulebook.plain: The lock arrangement is recommended; the spring and wire strength are required.

rulebook.title: Recommended lane-rope colour scheme
rulebook.statement: The colour arrangement is recommended as detailed in the event-specific subclauses. The permitted colour-variation condition is set out in 15.7.6.4.
rulebook.plain: Read the following colour layouts as recommendations; colour variations have their own mandatory condition.

rulebook.title: Olympic outer green ropes
rulebook.statement: For the Olympic layout, two green ropes are recommended for lanes 1 and 8.
rulebook.plain: The recommended outside Olympic racing-lane ropes are green.

rulebook.title: Olympic blue ropes
rulebook.statement: For the Olympic layout, four blue ropes are recommended for lanes 2, 3, 6 and 7.
rulebook.plain: Blue identifies the recommended intermediate Olympic lane-rope positions.

rulebook.title: Olympic centre yellow ropes
rulebook.statement: For the Olympic layout, three yellow ropes are recommended around lanes 4 and 5.
rulebook.plain: The recommended centre Olympic lane ropes are yellow.

rulebook.title: World Championship outer green ropes
rulebook.statement: At the World Aquatics Championships and World Aquatics Swimming Championships (25m), two green ropes are recommended for lanes 0 and 9.
rulebook.plain: The recommended outer ropes in the ten-lane championship layout are green.

rulebook.title: World Championship blue ropes
rulebook.statement: At those World Championships, six blue ropes are recommended for lanes 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8.
rulebook.plain: Blue marks the recommended intermediate rope positions in the ten-lane layout.

rulebook.title: World Championship centre yellow ropes
rulebook.statement: At those World Championships, three yellow ropes are recommended around lanes 4 and 5.
rulebook.plain: The recommended centre ropes are yellow.

rulebook.title: Other competitions: green ropes
rulebook.statement: For the illustrated layout at other competitions, two green ropes are recommended for lanes 1 and 8.
rulebook.plain: This is the recommended colour layout, not a requirement that every pool have eight racing lanes.

rulebook.title: Other competitions: blue ropes
rulebook.statement: For the illustrated layout at other competitions, four blue ropes are recommended for lanes 2, 3, 6 and 7.
rulebook.plain: The recommended intermediate ropes are blue.

rulebook.title: Other competitions: yellow ropes
rulebook.statement: For the illustrated layout at other competitions, three yellow ropes are recommended around lanes 4 and 5.
rulebook.plain: The recommended central ropes are yellow.

rulebook.title: Permitted alternative rope colours
rulebook.statement: Different lane-rope colours may be used, provided three colours distinguish the respective lane groups.
rulebook.plain: A pool may use a different palette, but must still distinguish the lane groups using three colours.

rulebook.title: Red rope sections at each wall
rulebook.statement: The lane-rope floats must be red for the first 5.0 m from each pool end.
rulebook.plain: The red end section identifies the final 5 m approaching a wall; it is not the 15 m underwater limit.

rulebook.title: One rope between lanes and required tension
rulebook.statement: There may be no more than one rope separating adjacent lanes. Each rope must be firmly tensioned within 1.0–1.2 kN.
rulebook.plain: Do not double up lane ropes between lanes; keep each rope within its specified tension range.

rulebook.title: Distinctive 15 m rope markers
rulebook.statement: Each lane rope must have floats of a contrasting colour at points 15 m from both end walls.
rulebook.plain: The 15 m rope markers identify the underwater-distance checkpoint measured from each wall.

rulebook.title: Midpoint marker in a 50 m pool
rulebook.statement: A 50 m pool must have distinctive lane-rope floats marking the 25 m midpoint, ordinarily using a contrasting colour.
rulebook.plain: The middle of a long-course length has its own rope marker; this does not create an extra underwater allowance.

rulebook.title: Optional soft lane numbers
rulebook.statement: Soft lane-number markers may be attached to ropes at both the starting and turning ends.
rulebook.plain: Rope-mounted lane numbers are permitted, but this clause does not require them.

rulebook.title: Stable, non-slip starting platform
rulebook.statement: The starting platform must be rigid without spring action. Its top must sit 0.50–0.75 m above the water and measure at least 0.50 m in each direction, with a slip-resistant finish.
rulebook.plain: The block must be stable, grippy, large enough, and within the specified height range.

rulebook.title: Block slope, back plate and gripping edges
rulebook.statement: The platform slope cannot exceed 10 degrees. An adjustable rear plate is optional. The block must allow a forward-start grip at the front and sides. Where the top is thicker than 0.04 m, recessed grips are recommended: at least 0.10 m across each side and 0.40 m across the front, cut to 0.03 m from the upper surface.
rulebook.plain: A rear foot wedge is allowed. The ability to grip the front and sides is required, while the detailed recessed-grip design is a recommendation.

rulebook.title: Backstroke and forward-start handgrips
rulebook.statement: Forward-start side grips are optional. Backstroke grips, in both horizontal and vertical arrangements, must be 0.30–0.60 m above the water. They must align parallel with the end wall and cannot project beyond its face.
rulebook.plain: Backstroke hands grip above the water, with no part of the grip sticking out past the wall into the course.

rulebook.title: Water depth in the block-start zone
rulebook.statement: A pool with starting blocks requires at least 1.35 m water depth through the zone beginning 1.0 m from the end wall and continuing to at least 6.0 m from that wall.
rulebook.plain: The specified depth must cover the whole start-entry zone. This facility dimension does not replace domestic safe-start requirements or an individual swimmer’s assessment.

rulebook.title: Displays beneath starting blocks
rulebook.statement: An electronic display may sit below a block, but during a backstroke start it must not flash or show moving figures.
rulebook.plain: A display must remain visually steady while backstrokers start.

rulebook.title: Visible block numbers
rulebook.statement: Each block must carry a clearly visible number on every side. Placing lane 0 at the right when viewed from the starting end is recommended; 50 m races may start at the opposite end. Touch panels may carry numbers at their upper or lower edge.
rulebook.plain: Read the visible block number. The recommended numbering viewpoint can differ for a 50 m race starting from the far end.

rulebook.title: Backstroke flags and 15 m side marks
rulebook.statement: A flagged rope must cross the pool at each end, supported 5.0 m from the end wall and positioned 1.8 m above the water. Distinctive 15.0 m marks are required on both pool sides and, where possible, on every lane rope.
rulebook.plain: Flags are 5 m from the wall in both 25 m and 50 m pools. They are a turning reference, separate from the 15 m underwater markers.

rulebook.title: Flag shape, spacing and signage
rulebook.statement: The triangular flags must have a 0.20 m edge attached to the rope and two other edges of 0.40 m each. Adjacent flags must be 0.25 m apart. Printed material or signage on them requires prior World Aquatics approval.
rulebook.plain: Flags have a specified triangular shape and spacing; printed flag designs have an approval requirement under this WA specification.

rulebook.title: Backstroke ledge specification
rulebook.statement: The WA facility standard requires backstroke ledges complying with the dimensions and adjustment limits in 15.10.1.1–15.10.1.3 and its accompanying diagram.
rulebook.plain: Use the specified ledge design where this facility standard applies. This does not by itself establish the equipment provision at every English domestic meet.

rulebook.title: Ledge adjustment above and below the water
rulebook.statement: The backstroke ledge must adjust through a range from 4 cm below to 4 cm above the water level. It cannot be used outside that range.
rulebook.plain: Set the ledge no more than 4 cm above or below the surface.

rulebook.title: Minimum ledge length
rulebook.statement: The backstroke ledge must be at least 60 cm long.
rulebook.plain: The usable ledge assembly must meet the 60 cm minimum length.

rulebook.title: Ledge height, width and slope
rulebook.statement: The ledge must have a height of 8 cm, a width of 2 cm and a slope of 10 degrees.
rulebook.plain: The ledge profile has fixed dimensions; see the labelled diagram for the direction of each measurement.

rulebook.title: Competition water temperature
rulebook.statement: Pool water must be within 25.0–28.0 degrees Celsius.
rulebook.plain: This facility standard sets the permitted water-temperature range.

rulebook.title: Stable water level during competition
rulebook.statement: The water surface level must remain steady during competition, without appreciable movement.
rulebook.plain: Pool operation must not create a changing level or a significant current.

rulebook.title: Water circulation on competition and training days
rulebook.statement: Inflow and outflow must be regulated at the size-specific rates below on training and competition days, to maintain level and clarity while accounting for applicable health requirements.
rulebook.plain: The stated circulation ranges are tied to pool length; they do not displace public-health requirements.

rulebook.title: 50 m pool circulation rate
rulebook.statement: For a 50 m pool, the regulated inflow and outflow range is 220–250 cubic metres per hour on the training and competition days covered by 15.11.2.2.
rulebook.plain: Long-course circulation uses the 220–250 m³/h range under this specification.

rulebook.title: 33.333 m pool circulation rate
rulebook.statement: For a 33.333 m pool, the regulated inflow and outflow range is 150–180 cubic metres per hour on the days covered by 15.11.2.2.
rulebook.plain: This separate circulation range belongs to a 33.333 m pool.

rulebook.title: 25 m pool circulation rate
rulebook.statement: For a 25 m pool, the regulated inflow and outflow range is 120–150 cubic metres per hour on the days covered by 15.11.2.2.
rulebook.plain: Short-course circulation uses the 120–150 m³/h range under this specification.

rulebook.title: Water circulation in ordinary use
rulebook.statement: Outside competition, daily water inflow and outflow must comply with the health regulations of the country concerned.
rulebook.plain: Normal pool operation follows the local public-health rules.

rulebook.title: Limit on current and turbulence
rulebook.statement: The specified turnover rates must not produce appreciable turbulence or current. The current criterion is movement of a floating basketball containing 6 litres of water more than 1.25 m in one direction during 60 seconds.
rulebook.plain: The weighted basketball test checks whether the circulation is producing too much directional movement.

rulebook.title: Practical basketball current test
rulebook.statement: Place a basketball prepared as in 15.11.2.4 at the centre of a 2.5 m square formed using floating lines across a lane. The test passes if the ball touches none of the four surrounding ropes within 60 seconds.
rulebook.plain: Mark out the square, start the ball centrally, and observe it for a full minute.

rulebook.title: Recommended current-test locations
rulebook.statement: The test should be performed eight times: at each end in lanes 1, 3, 6 and 8. The ball should begin 5 m from the relevant end wall or bulkhead.
rulebook.plain: The recommended checks sample both ends and several positions across the pool; this clause uses “should”.

rulebook.title: Lighting at Olympic and WA events
rulebook.statement: For the Olympic Games and World Aquatics Events, illumination measured from the pool deck must be at least 1,500 lux across the entire pool.
rulebook.plain: The named events require the higher light level throughout the pool.

rulebook.title: Lighting at other competitions
rulebook.statement: At other competitions, illumination over the blocks and turning ends must be at least 600 lux, measured from deck level.
rulebook.plain: This provision specifies minimum lighting at the start and turn ends for other competitions.

rulebook.title: Floor-line colour, width and length
rulebook.statement: The centre of each lane must have a dark, contrasting floor line 0.20–0.30 m wide. Its total length must be 46.0 m in a 50 m pool or 21.0 m in a 25 m pool.
rulebook.plain: The floor line stops short of both walls, leaving 2 m at each end.

rulebook.title: Floor T markers and lane centres
rulebook.statement: The central floor line must stop 2.0 m from each end wall, ending in a perpendicular crossbar 1.0 m long and as wide as the line. Lane and marking centre points must be 2.5 m apart.
rulebook.plain: The T warns you that the wall is 2 m away. It is different from the overhead 5 m flags and the 15 m marker.

rulebook.title: Wall and touch-panel targets
rulebook.statement: A vertical target of the same width as the floor line must be centred on each end wall or touch panel. It must continue from the deck edge to the pool floor, with a maximum extent of 3 m. Its perpendicular crossbar must be 0.5 m long and centred 0.3 m below the water.
rulebook.plain: The wall target helps identify the lane centre. Its crossbar sits 30 cm below the surface.

rulebook.title: 15 m floor crossbars and older pools
rulebook.statement: In 25 m and 50 m pools built on or after 1 January 2006, each lane must have a perpendicular 0.5 m crossbar at the 15 m point from each end. Where a crossbar is present, measure the 15 m distance to its centre.
rulebook.plain: An older pool may lack this floor marking under the stated exception. The swimming rule’s 15 m limit still applies.

rulebook.title: Bulkhead used as an end wall
rulebook.statement: A bulkhead serving as an end wall must span the course width and provide a solid, smooth, stable, vertical, non-slip face suitable for touch panels, extending at least 0.8 m below and 0.3 m above the water. It must have no hazardous openings into which a swimmer’s hands, feet or digits could enter. Officials must be able to move along it without creating appreciable current or turbulence.
rulebook.plain: A movable wall must function safely as a genuine racing wall and remain stable while officials use it.

rulebook.title: Separation from a diving pool at named events
rulebook.statement: At the Olympic Games and World Aquatics Championships, when the swimming and diving pools share an area, the separation rules depend on the pools’ construction date.
rulebook.plain: The next two clauses apply to those named events when the two pools occupy the same area.

rulebook.title: Separation for pools built from 2014
rulebook.statement: For the shared-area pools covered by 15.15 and constructed on or after 1 January 2014, the minimum separation is 8 m; a 10 m separation is preferred.
rulebook.plain: Eight metres is the requirement, while ten metres is the preference.

rulebook.title: Separation for pools built before 2014
rulebook.statement: For the shared-area pools covered by 15.15 and constructed before 1 January 2014, the minimum separation is 5.0 m.
rulebook.plain: The older-pool provision permits a smaller minimum gap.

rulebook.title: What electronic officiating equipment records
rulebook.statement: Automatic and semi-automatic officiating equipment measure each competitor’s elapsed race time and establish relative finishing positions.
rulebook.plain: The system supplies both times and the order in which swimmers finish.

rulebook.title: Starter initiates electronic timing
rulebook.statement: In automatic and semi-automatic systems, the Starter manually initiates the timing.
rulebook.plain: Both system types start from the Starter’s action.

rulebook.title: Automatic finish and video backup
rulebook.statement: With automatic equipment, a competitor’s contact with the finish touch panel stops that lane’s clock. The usual backup is video timing calibrated to hundredths of a second.
rulebook.plain: The swimmer’s finish touch records the primary time; the described backup uses calibrated video.

rulebook.title: Two semi-automatic timing arrangements
rulebook.statement: Semi-automatic equipment may use swimmer-operated finish panels backed up by officials’ buttons, or may use officials’ buttons when panels are absent or not functioning.
rulebook.plain: Semi-automatic timing includes the manual-button arrangements specified in the next two subclauses.

rulebook.title: Panel timing with button backup
rulebook.statement: One semi-automatic arrangement stops a competitor’s time through finish-panel contact, with Timekeepers’ manual button presses at the wall touch providing the backup.
rulebook.plain: A panel is the main stop, while an official’s button provides the backup stop.

rulebook.title: Button timing without usable panels
rulebook.statement: If touch panels are unavailable or not working, Timekeepers stop each competitor’s official electronic time by pressing a button when that swimmer touches the finish wall.
rulebook.plain: An official judges the touch and presses the stop button.

rulebook.title: Starter activation
rulebook.statement: Automatic and semi-automatic equipment must be activated by the Starter.
rulebook.plain: The Starter triggers the timing system.

rulebook.title: Protected deck cabling
rulebook.statement: Automatic and semi-automatic timing installations must not leave wires or cables exposed on the deck.
rulebook.plain: Keep timing cables safely protected around the pool.

rulebook.title: Results by place and lane
rulebook.statement: The system must be able to show all recorded lane information in both finishing-position order and lane order.
rulebook.plain: Officials must be able to view results by placing or by lane number.

rulebook.title: Readable digital times
rulebook.statement: The equipment must provide a readily readable digital presentation of each competitor’s time.
rulebook.plain: The time display must be clear to read.

rulebook.title: Timing precision
rulebook.statement: The equipment must measure accurately to one hundredth of a second.
rulebook.plain: The specified accuracy is 0.01 seconds.

rulebook.title: No interference from timing equipment
rulebook.statement: The installation must not obstruct starts, turns or operation of the pool overflow system.
rulebook.plain: Timing equipment must leave swimmers and pool drainage able to function properly.

rulebook.title: Starter microphone
rulebook.statement: A microphone must be available to the Starter for spoken instructions.
rulebook.plain: Starting commands are delivered through the microphone.

rulebook.title: Pistol signal transducer
rulebook.statement: When a starting pistol is used, it must operate with a transducer.
rulebook.plain: A pistol start requires the specified signal-conversion device.

rulebook.title: Equal starting sound at every block
rulebook.statement: The microphone and pistol transducer must feed loudspeakers at every starting block, giving all competitors the instructions and start signal at equal volume and at the same time.
rulebook.plain: Every swimmer must receive the starting information equally and simultaneously.

rulebook.title: False-start detection installation
rulebook.statement: The starting system must include installed false-start detection equipment.
rulebook.plain: This is an equipment requirement within the WA facility specification; it does not itself describe how every domestic meet is staffed or equipped.

rulebook.title: Touch-panel dimensions
rulebook.statement: Each touch panel must be at least 2.4 m wide and 0.9 m high. Its thickness at the instant contact closes and stops the time must be 0.01 m.
rulebook.plain: The panel must meet the minimum face size and the specified compressed contact thickness.

rulebook.title: Panel position, separate lane circuits and target
rulebook.statement: A touch panel must extend 0.3 m above and 0.6 m below the water. Each lane must have an independent electronic connection for individual control and maintenance. The face must be brightly coloured and carry the required end-wall target marking.
rulebook.plain: Panels straddle the waterline and work independently by lane. Their visible wall targets must be retained.
rulebook.issue: The printed clause points to 15.14 for wall markings, but the lane and wall markings are described in 15.13. This app flags that cross-reference mismatch rather than silently treating 15.14 as a marking specification.

rulebook.title: Fixed central panel placement
rulebook.statement: A touch panel must be fixed in the centre of its lane while installed. A portable design is permitted so it can be removed outside competition use.
rulebook.plain: A removable panel is allowed, but it must be securely fixed in its correct racing position.

rulebook.title: Touch-panel sensitivity
rulebook.statement: Water turbulence must not activate a panel, but a light hand contact must activate it. The panel’s upper edge must also respond to contact.
rulebook.plain: The panel should register a light hand touch, including at its top edge, without triggering from moving water alone. A recorded time does not by itself prove that the touch complied with the stroke rule.

rulebook.title: Touch-panel markings and border
rulebook.statement: Panel targets must match and align over the pool’s existing markings. A black border 0.025 m wide must define the panel edges and perimeter.
rulebook.plain: The panel’s target should line up with the pool target and have a visible 2.5 cm black border.

rulebook.title: Touch-panel safety
rulebook.statement: Touch panels must present neither an electrical-shock hazard nor sharp edges.
rulebook.plain: The panel must be safe to touch and turn against.

rulebook.title: Semi-automatic operation
rulebook.statement: Semi-automatic systems must follow the timing arrangements described in 15.16.1.
rulebook.plain: Use one of the defined panel-and-button or button-only operating arrangements.

rulebook.title: Button backup at WA events
rulebook.statement: World Aquatics may choose a semi-automatic backup for automatic equipment at its events if each lane has one button operated by its own official. Additional Finish Judges are then unnecessary. An Inspector of Turns may operate a button.
rulebook.plain: This is an optional WA event backup arrangement with a separate official for every lane button.

rulebook.title: Printing and previous results
rulebook.statement: Automatic and semi-automatic equipment must have facilities to print information and retrieve earlier race results electronically.
rulebook.plain: Officials need access to a printed record and previous results.

rulebook.title: Spectator results display
rulebook.statement: An electronic spectator display must be available with automatic and semi-automatic equipment.
rulebook.plain: Race information must be available on an electronic display for spectators.

rulebook.title: Relay take-off equipment and video support
rulebook.statement: Relay changeover judging to 0.01 seconds must be available. Organisers should consult the manufacturer about any changeover time differential. Installed overhead video may supplement the automatic system’s take-off judgement.
rulebook.plain: Use the equipment’s proper operating guidance. This does not create a freely chosen tolerance or make overhead video mandatory.

rulebook.title: Automatic lap count
rulebook.statement: An automatic lap counter must be available with the electronic officiating equipment.
rulebook.plain: The equipment package includes an automatic count of completed laps.

rulebook.title: Split-time display
rulebook.statement: The electronic officiating equipment must provide a way to read split times.
rulebook.plain: Intermediate times must be available to read.

rulebook.title: Computer summaries
rulebook.statement: Computer-generated summaries must be available with the electronic officiating equipment.
rulebook.plain: The system must support a computer summary of recorded information.

rulebook.title: Correction after erroneous contact
rulebook.statement: The equipment must provide a way to correct results caused by an erroneous touch.
rulebook.plain: An accidental or incorrect trigger must be capable of correction through the system.

rulebook.title: Rechargeable battery capability
rulebook.statement: The equipment must have the capability for automatic operation using rechargeable batteries.
rulebook.plain: A rechargeable-battery operating option must be available.

rulebook.title: Elite-event spectator display size
rulebook.statement: At the Olympic Games and World Aquatics Championships, the electronic spectator display used with automatic equipment must measure at least 7.5 m wide by 4.5 m high.
rulebook.plain: This large display minimum belongs to the named elite events.

rulebook.title: Elite-event control room
rulebook.statement: At the Olympic Games and World Aquatics Championships, the air-conditioned control room must be at least 6.0 m by 3.0 m and lie 3.0–5.0 m from the finish wall, with a continuously unobstructed finish view. The Referee must have easy access during competition, and the room must be capable of being secured at other times.
rulebook.plain: The named events require a suitably sized, secure control room with an uninterrupted finish view and ready referee access.

rulebook.title: Elite-event video officiating support
rulebook.statement: At the Olympic Games and World Aquatics Championships, video recordings must be supplied for initiating or confirming stroke-infraction calls and helping the Referee assess pool-deck calls.
rulebook.plain: Video forms part of the officiating provision at these named events; the rule is not a claim that every English meet has video review.

rulebook.title: Timing-room sightline and advertising limits
rulebook.statement: Timekeepers must have a clear view from the timing room to the poolside finish end. On that side, advertising panels and LED walls must leave at least 2 m clear from the finish wall and must not exceed 46 m in length.
rulebook.plain: Advertising must not block the timing team’s view of the finish.

rulebook.title: Underwater broadcast equipment
rulebook.statement: When broadcasters use underwater video equipment, the Management Committee must ensure remote operation. The equipment must not obstruct swimmers’ route or view, alter the pool setup or specification, or hide required pool markings or applicable World Aquatics markings.
rulebook.plain: Broadcast cameras must work without changing or obstructing the racing environment.

rulebook.title: Swimming-specific safety rules supplement Part One
rulebook.statement: The swimming medical and safety provisions apply at the Olympic Games, World Aquatics Events and other swimming competitions under these regulations. They supplement the medical and safety requirements in Part One section 8.
rulebook.plain: Both the general medical framework and these swimming-specific provisions apply within the stated competition scope. This table covers Part Two; it does not reproduce the separate Part One chapter.

rulebook.title: Plan for training before competition
rulebook.statement: When preparing and implementing the Medical Plan, the Local Organising Committee should account for the particular requirements of pre-competition swimming training described in 16.2.1 and 16.2.2.
rulebook.plain: Medical planning needs to cover training and warm-up periods as well as races.

rulebook.title: Warm-up attendance and collision risk
rulebook.statement: The plan should account for the usual morning and afternoon/evening competition sessions and athletes arriving about 2.5–3 hours before racing to train and warm up. Many swimmers may be in the water, moving around the deck, exercising or stretching. Different strokes and isolated race-skills practice, such as starts, increase the risk of collisions and accidents in and around the water.
rulebook.plain: Plan staffing and supervision around the busy period before each session; the arrival times describe likely activity, not a mandatory athlete reporting deadline.

rulebook.title: Adjust lifeguard numbers to warm-up demand
rulebook.statement: At major competitions, especially high numbers of athletes may use the warm-up area. The organising committee’s medical team must adapt lifeguard numbers so athletes in the different pools are appropriately safeguarded.
rulebook.plain: The lifeguard provision must reflect how many swimmers are using each pool.

rulebook.title: Position of the field-of-play medical station
rulebook.statement: The field-of-play medical station should be as near as practicable to the point where athletes leave the competition pool, while keeping the mixed zone on the deck unobstructed.
rulebook.plain: Place medical support close to the pool exit without blocking the athletes’ route through the mixed zone.

rulebook.title: Daily rescue practice for swimming conditions
rulebook.statement: The organising committee’s medical team should arrange daily practice of water-retrieval skills by lifeguards during the competition. Practice should consider swimming-specific obstacles, including lane ropes that can impede access and affect the extraction point.
rulebook.plain: The recommendation is to rehearse rescue in the actual swimming-pool arrangement, including the lane ropes.

rulebook.title: Recommended lifeguard positions at the competition pool
rulebook.statement: The organising committee’s medical team should position three lifeguards at the competition pool: two beside the field-of-play medical station and one on the opposite side.
rulebook.plain: This provision recommends a three-person deployment pattern; it does not override the duty to adjust staffing for the number of swimmers and pools in use.

rulebook.title: English referee authority and event conditions
rulebook.statement: Within Swim England competition, the referee controls the officials and enforces the applicable Swim England regulations, technical rules and the promoter’s conditions.
rulebook.plain: The referee oversees the competition. The event’s conditions matter alongside the technical rules.

rulebook.title: English referee intervention
rulebook.statement: The referee may intervene during the competition to ensure that the applicable regulations are observed.
rulebook.plain: The referee can step in to enforce the competition rules.

rulebook.title: Which technical rules apply in England
rulebook.statement: Subject to the stated domestic provisions, swimming under Swim England jurisdiction uses the relevant World Aquatics rules, including its swimming rules and applicable bylaws. Published Swim England health and safety guidance takes precedence where it conflicts with those technical rules.
rulebook.plain: Use the applicable World Aquatics swimming rules together with English provisions. A technical diving-start rule does not override Swim England safety requirements.

updates.title: Breaststroke turn: rotate before any kick
updates.label: August clarification · 6 August 2026
updates.summary: You may leave a breaststroke turn on your back, but must rotate past vertical onto the breast before any kick. The body must be on the breast when the first arm stroke begins.
points: “Any kick” includes the permitted dolphin/butterfly kick in the pullout. Do not teach a dolphin kick while the swimmer is still on the back after the turn.
The first arm stroke must begin on the breast. The August clarification adds the explicit condition on kicking; the February wording alone misses that condition.

This departure permission follows a legal breaststroke turn touch. A backstroke-to-breaststroke medley change still requires the outgoing backstroke finish touch on the back before the next stroke begins.
updates.scope: This states the latest World Aquatics guidance. Its specific English application following the August commentary has not been independently confirmed; the app keeps that issue visible.

updates.title: Freestyle finish: conditional submersion in the final 5m
updates.label: February change · August clarification
updates.summary: Once the head has passed the final 5m mark, complete submersion is permitted when reaching for the finish wall.
points: This is a finish-reaching allowance, not permission to swim the whole final 5m underwater.
It does not apply to the approach to a turn and does not change the head-surfacing limit after a start or turn.
The finish wall must still be touched. Backstroke already had a final-5m finish allowance; the freestyle provision is a 2026 addition.
updates.scope: English adoption of the February package is verified on the dates below. The August commentary reinforces the finish-reaching condition already present in February; a separate English application date for that commentary has not been confirmed.

updates.title: Butterfly finish: submersion still needs a legal touch
updates.label: February change · August clarification
updates.summary: The final-5m finish-reaching submersion allowance also applies to butterfly. Both separated hands must still touch at the same time.
points: The head must have passed the final 5m mark, and the swimmer must be reaching for the finish. This is not an approach-to-turn exception.
The February rulebook contains the allowance in 8.6. The August commentary calls the finish point 8.6.7; the lookup accepts both references.
“Separated” means the hands are not stacked. A visible gap or equal hand height is not required.
updates.scope: English adoption of the February package is verified. August reinforces its finish-reaching condition; a separate English application date for that commentary has not been confirmed. The submersion allowance does not replace the two-hand finish.

updates.title: Butterfly turn: on the breast after leaving the wall
updates.label: August clarification · 6 August 2026
updates.summary: For butterfly, the body must be on the breast after leaving the turn wall. Do not delay that position until the first arm stroke.
points: The commentary removes the reference to turns from 8.1; that clause’s first-arm-stroke test remains for the start.
For the turn, clarified 8.2 puts the body-position requirement at departure from the wall.
Do not apply the breaststroke departure permission to butterfly.
updates.scope: This states the latest World Aquatics guidance. Its specific English application following the August commentary has not been independently confirmed; the app keeps that issue visible.

updates.title: 400m freestyle: lap cards and warning signal
updates.label: February change · 2026
updates.summary: Lap recording, lap cards and the warning bell or whistle now include individual 400m freestyle, as well as 800m and 1500m.
points: Turn inspectors at both ends record completed lengths. At the turning end, lap cards show odd numbers for the lengths still to swim; permitted electronic displays may be used.
At the starting end, give the warning with two pool lengths plus 5m remaining: 55m in a 25m pool or 105m in a 50m pool.
Repeat the signal after the turn until the swimmer reaches the 5m mark on the lane rope.
updates.scope: In England the February package applies at Level 1 meets from 27 March 2026 and at all other levels, including unlicensed meets, from 11 May 2026. This includes club championships held under those rules.

updates.title: Injury tape and nasal strips: read the August guidance
updates.label: February change · August clarification
updates.summary: The February injury-tape permission covers one or two fingers or toes, including binding two together. August guidance extends injury-treatment or protection tape to other body parts.
points: The reason for the wider taping permission remains treating or protecting an injury. It is not unrestricted permission to use tape for performance assistance.
For 14.2, the commentary explains that the banned adhesive substance means glue. Tape and nasal strips are not treated as glue and may be used under that clause.
Other equipment restrictions still apply; tape or a nasal strip must not be used to evade them.
updates.scope: This states the latest World Aquatics guidance. Its specific English application following the August commentary has not been independently confirmed; the app keeps that issue visible.

updates.title: Early starts: referee review of official footage
updates.label: August clarification · 6 August 2026
updates.summary: When the relevant official equipment is available, the referee reviews the footage to verify an early-start disqualification. Following that review, the referee and starter need not agree.
points: The ordinary visual route requires both the starter and referee to observe and confirm that the swimmer initiated the start before the signal.
The equipment-review route is different: the August commentary confirms that concurrence is not required and that the referee’s decision following that review is final.
This concerns official equipment and the referee’s process. It does not make a spectator’s video an automatic replacement for officiating evidence.
updates.scope: February 2.3.6 already distinguishes the two evidence routes. August clarifies the referee’s decision after review; an English notice specifically applying that August clarification has not been independently verified.

updates.title: When the February rules took effect in England
updates.label: England implementation · March / May 2026
updates.summary: Level 1 meets adopted the revised rules from 27 March 2026. All other levels, including unlicensed meets, followed from 11 May 2026.
points: Use the event’s governing rules and conditions alongside these implementation dates.
The March/May notice establishes adoption of the February regulations. It does not by itself establish how every August clarification was subsequently applied in England.
updates.scope: The relevant English safety provisions continue to take precedence where they conflict with a technical rule.

updates.title: Relay semi-finals: an erroneous provision is withdrawn
updates.label: August correction · 6 August 2026
updates.summary: World Aquatics says the printed relay semi-final provision, 3.3.5, was included in error and is not to be applied.
points: Swimming relay events governed by these regulations do not have semi-finals.
The commentary says the provision will be removed in the next annual revision. Its appearance in the February PDF is not a reason to apply it now.
updates.scope: The master table preserves the code with a clear withdrawal explanation, so a code lookup does not teach the erroneous procedure.
